faq.q: How much does a split system cost in Canberra?
faq.a: It depends on the room, the system and where the outdoor unit goes — which is exactly why we quote on site rather than over the phone. The quote is free either way.

faq.q: How long does an install take?
faq.a: A single split system is usually a straightforward day. Ducted takes longer — we'll give you a realistic timeframe as part of the quote.

faq.q: Do you service what you install?
faq.a: Yes, and we'll also service or repair a system someone else installed.

faq.q: How often should I service my system?
faq.a: Once a year is the general rule, more often for a system that runs hard through both a Canberra summer and winter. Regular servicing is also what keeps a workmanship warranty valid.

Canberra
servicePages.sub: Runs on Canberra's dry summer air for a fraction of the running cost of refrigerated cooling.
servicePages.intro: Canberra's summers are hot but dry — exactly the climate evaporative cooling is built for. It costs a lot less to run than refrigerated air, and it keeps fresh air moving through the house rather than sealing it up.

_needsConfirming.sameDayService: The brief's seasonal urgency banner ("Same-day repairs / call-out") was NOT built. Nothing on First Point's own site claims same-day service, and the brief said to confirm this before using that wording. Confirm with the owner, then it can be added.
_needsConfirming.pricing: No dollar figures anywhere — First Point publish none. The pricing guide (calculator section) is wired up in 'quote' mode with no numbers. Give real ranges (e.g. 'split install from $X') and these become priced tiers.
_needsConfirming.email: sales@firstpointac.com is their real, current email (used on their own homepage and contact page) but it does not match their own domain, firstpointairconditioning.com.au — the same mismatch exists on their live site today, it wasn't introduced here. Confirm which is correct before publishing.
_needsConfirming.warranty: Their own site states both a '12-Month Installation Warranty' and a 'comprehensive 5-year warranty' in the same breath, without saying what the 5-year covers (reads like the manufacturer's parts warranty, not workmanship). Used only the confirmed 12-month workmanship figure on the page; the 5-year claim needs the owner to clarify what it actually covers before it goes anywhere.
_needsConfirming.ownerName: No owner or technician name is published anywhere — About page, team page, contact page, Localsearch or Google. Copy is written in the business's own voice ('we', 'the team') instead of a named person. If there's a name to use, the page gets more personal with it.
_needsConfirming.licensing: No licence, certification or 'licensed & insured' claim is published anywhere on their site, so the brief's 'Licensed & insured' trust-strip item was left out rather than assumed. If they hold ARC/ACT trade licences, add the numbers and this becomes a strong trust signal.
_needsConfirming.photos: Zero real photos of First Point's team, vans or installs exist anywhere online. Hero and gallery use CC0 stock, clearly labelled as samples. Needs real Canberra job photos before this goes anywhere near live.
_needsConfirming.reviews: Only 4 Google reviews exist (via Localsearch, which mirrors Google) — genuinely all of them, not a curated subset. More reviews would strengthen this a lot; none were invented to pad the count.
_needsConfirming.secondPhoneNumber: Their own site also lists a mobile, 0488 025 856, alongside 02 6100 2247. The brief said one number sitewide, no exceptions, so only 02 6100 2247 is used anywhere on this page.
